FY2024/25 revenue and operating margin: not found in available tier-1 sources; FY2023/24 revenue implied at £2,028.5 million from prior-year MoD reporting references, though the exact 2025 figure is obscured by qualification issues. The National Audit Office issued a qualified opinion on the MoD's 2024-25 accounts due to a lack of supporting analysis for £6.13 billion in AWE capital project assets. 100% UK geography (Aldermaston and Burghfield sites). No consensus applicable - government body.

companies.strategic_move: Two strategic tracks: (1) Aldermaston Asset Remediation and Safety Return Plan - detailed in the statutory Annual Report and Accounts published January 29, 2026; the NAO's £6.13bn qualified-opinion finding on AWE's assets under construction is the direct explanation for the accounting/traceability gaps flagged in the financial snapshot; the stated outcome is returning the nuclear weapons infrastructure site safely to routine technical operations after intense regulatory scrutiny. (2) Environment and Space Sustainability Policy Activation - published alongside AWE's initial TCFD disclosure framework in early 2026, aligning long-term public production facilities and defense works with UK government net-zero targets; this is a forward-looking regulatory-alignment move with no near-term impact on the cost-recovery funding model.

competitive_landscape.engagement: Provides high-performance computing system validation, highly restricted modeling environments, and asset lifecycle tools to monitor nuclear infrastructure projects.
